caseno:
Writ Petition No. 3078 of 1992, Writ Petition No. 3733 of 1992
and Writ Petition No. 3734 of 1992.
lawyer:
Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed with Mirza Hossain Haider, Advocates ----- For the Petitioners 
Ziaur Rahman Khan, Advocate ----- For Respondent No.1 
Aminul Hoque Attorney General with Md. Altafur Rahman. AAG and Mir Hashmat Ali, AAG ----- For Respondent No.2.
parties:
Sadeque Uddin Ahmed &others ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakhya (formerly Dhaka Improvement Trust) and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment: 9. Mr. Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, the learned Counsel appeared for the petitioner while the learned Counsel Mr. Ziaur Rahman Khan appeared for the respondent No. 1 RAJUK and Mr. Aminul Hoque, the learned Attorney-General appeared for the Government All of them made lengthy and elaborate submissions touching the merit of the claim and points of law involved in the matter of requisition and acquisition of land. Mr. Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed after taking us through the petition, affidavits-in-opposition and replies thereof vehemently assailed the impugned notification published by the respondent No. 1 inviting application for allotment of the land which was admittedly requisitioned under section 93A of the Town Improvement Act, 1953 in LA Case No. 138/61-62 and part compensation was paid and received by the owners as advance. The contention of Mr. Mahbubuddin Ahmed is that the lands of plots of Mouza Joar Shahara as mentioned in the applications originally belonged to the predecessors of the petitioners and though it was requisitioned for the purpose of development of 1000 acres of land in Greater Dhaka Development Scheme it was not utilised for over 50 years by the respondent No. 1 since the date of requisition and subsequently the scheme having been revised, reducing the area to 832 acres and thereafter to 524 acres, and the lands of plot of mouza Joar Shahara as claimed by the petitioners having fallen outside the revised scheme the proposed allotment of said land to others vide impugned notification on the plea of development of Nikunja Residential Area is without any lawful authority. In support of the claim of the petitioner in the land the learned Counsel for the petitioners annexed photo copy of the DP Khatian and photo copy of the map alleged to have been prepared by DIT. These maps and papers having not been produced earlier in any court or authority cannot be taken as a proof of the claim of the petitioners without evidence. The learned Counsel next submitted that the land was requisitioned in the year 1961-62 and more than 30 years have elapsed and the DIT having kept the land unutilised for such a long period has violated the mandate of law to start and accomplish the work 'forthwith' as provided under section 51A(4) of the Act. It is also contended that the petitioners having been deprived from utilising their land without getting full compensation, there has been violation of fundamental right of a citizen as guaranteed under Article 42 of the Constitution. The learned Counsel submitted that the land in question remained unutilized for more than 3 decades without payment of full compensation and now is going to be used for a purpose other than the purpose for which it was requisitioned, particularly when the authority themselves found that the land in excess of 832 or 524 acres is not necessary for implementation of the development plan or for the improvement of Dhaka City for which it was requisitioned. The learned Counsel has drawn our attention to Annexure-G in which the Deputy Secretary of the Government of East Pakistan (Revenue Department) communicated to the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka on 18.6.70 that 522 acres of land involved in LA Case No. 138/61-62 of the DIT should be retained and acquired and the proceeding should be finalised without loss of time. With regard to the question of realisation of compensation of land from the owners in respect of LA Case No. 138/61-62 by the DIT financial involvement was being examined and the Deputy Commissioner was directed to go ahead with the acquisition proceeding for 542 acres of land. Mr. Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed submitted that sufficient indication was there that the rest of the land was not necessary for the scheme and stood released. From the reading of Annexure-G it does not appear that the land in excess of the 524 acres were released or even sought to be released. The main ground urged by Mr. Khondker Mahbubuddin is that before acquisition proceeding is complete no property can vest absolutely under section 93A(4)(h) and in the instant case acquisition proceeding has never started. On the contrary, it was found by DIT that the excess land is not necessary for the purpose of the scheme and therefore, the land of the petitioners cannot be retained for an uncertain period without utilising, nor it can be utilised for purpose other than the scheme for which it was requisitioned. The learned Counsel, therefore, urged that unless acquired under due process of law the requisitioned land kept unutilised for such a long period cannot be the subject matter of allotment or lease to others.
